From 702d1e81feae70aa16ca364b4d2d95ccad801022 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Terry Zhou <bjzhou@marvell.com>
Date: Wed, 23 May 2018 10:44:05 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] pinctrl: armada-37xx: Fix spurious irq management

Until now, if we found spurious irq in irq_handler, we only updated the
status in register but not the status in the code. Due to this the system
will got stuck dues to the infinite loop

[gregory.clement@bootlin.com: update comment and add fix and stable tags]
Fixes: 30ac0d3b0702 ("pinctrl: armada-37xx: Add edge both type gpio irq support")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Terry Zhou <bjzhou@marvell.com>
Reviewed-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Gregory CLEMENT <gregory.clement@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c b/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
index 0f1eafba0ded..674ffdf8103c 100644
--- a/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
+++ b/drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c
@@ -666,12 +666,13 @@ static void armada_37xx_irq_handler(struct irq_desc *desc)
 					writel(1 << hwirq,
 					       info->base +
 					       IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
-					continue;
+					goto update_status;
 				}
 			}
 
 			generic_handle_irq(virq);
 
+update_status:
 			/* Update status in case a new IRQ appears */
 			spin_lock_irqsave(&info->irq_lock, flags);
 			status = readl_relaxed(info->base +
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/pinctrl/mvebu/pinctrl-armada-37xx.c`**
   - The line `continue;` was replaced with `goto update_status;` within the `armada_37xx_irq_handler` function. This change alters the flow of the function to ensure that when a spurious IRQ is detected, the code will jump to the `update_status` label instead of continuing the loop. 
   - The `update_status` label is introduced to handle the updating of the IRQ status in the code, ensuring that the status is correctly reflected in the system.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the `pinctrl-armada-37xx.c` file addresses a bug related to spurious IRQ management. Previously, when a spurious IRQ was detected, the handler would only update the status in the hardware register but not in the software state, leading to potential infinite loops and system hangs. By redirecting the flow to the `update_status` section, the patch ensures that the IRQ status is updated correctly in both the hardware and software, thus preventing the system from getting stuck. This change is crucial for maintaining the stability and reliability of the IRQ handling mechanism in the system.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
writel(1 << hwirq, info->base + IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
continue;
```
Reason:
The handler acknowledges a spurious IRQ by writing to the IRQ_STATUS register but does not update the software status in the code. This results in the handler continuously processing the same spurious IRQ without exiting the loop, leading to an infinite loop and causing the system to become unresponsive.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
goto update_status;
```
```c
status = readl_relaxed(info->base + IRQ_STATUS + 4 * i);
```
Reason:
The addition of the `goto update_status;` statement ensures that after acknowledging a spurious IRQ, the handler updates the software status by reading the IRQ_STATUS register again. This prevents the infinite loop by allowing the handler to check for new IRQs and exit if none are present, thus maintaining system responsiveness.
